verdict: Raw agreement 23.6%, Cohen's kappa -0.0013 (worse than chance). But the reference model is degenerate on radio: it assigns one quadrant to 82% of clips. On CREMA-D it works normally (81.7% vs a 58.3% baseline, largest class 61%), so the failure is domain transfer in the *reference*, not evidence about our scoring. This comparison cannot adjudicate either way - it is reported because the attempt was made, not because it settles anything.
why_kappa: Raw agreement is misleading here: both models over-produce one or two quadrants, so a large share of agreement happens by accident. Kappa subtracts the agreement expected from the marginal distributions.
